findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: The class was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` whose `evaluate` returned `[]` into `StatefulDetectorHandler[...]` with only `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and now `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and this class implements none of them. `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type `metric_alert_fire` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` instead of evaluating to nothing. `process_detectors` has no guard around that property, so one such detector aborts processing of the whole detector list. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` comment is also stale, since the class now claims to be stateful. Either keep the no-op `DetectorHandler` (returning `{}`) until the real implementation exists, or implement the abstract methods.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". The return type is now `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, keyed by group key. The new abstract `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook has no docstring either. A subclass author has nothing saying what `event_data` must contain (event_id, project_id, timestamp, and so on) or how the hook is called.

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with a value that differs from the evaluated value, so value passthrough is untested
findings.body: The mock `build_occurrence_and_event_data` ignores `value`. The tests build expected occurrences with a hard-coded `6` even when the evaluated value is different: group_2 is 10 here, `test_results_on_change` uses 100, and `test_dedupe` uses 8. The tests would still pass if `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value, the wrong group key, or the wrong priority to the hook. Nothing asserts the arguments the hook receives. Either have the mock encode `value` in the occurrence, for example in `evidence_data`, or add a test that asserts the hook's call arguments.
